post.caption:
A spacesuit has to hold pressure, supply oxygen, scrub carbon dioxide, manage a temperature swing of hundreds of degrees and stop micrometeorites, which is why it is built in layers from a water-cooled garment outward. The hardest part is mechanical: a pressurised suit resists bending, so an inflated glove behaves like a stiff balloon that wants to stay open. Every finger movement fights that pressure, hands tire within hours, and gloves remain the least solved part of the design.
